description: AIIR negative encoding vectors. Each vector shows a WRONG way to produce canonical JSON and the CORRECT way. Implementers can test their encoder against known misencoding traps.

vectors.description: WRONG: top-level keys in insertion order instead of sorted — the hash would be different
vectors.wrong_approach: Using insertion-order key serialization instead of sort_keys=True
vectors.trap: Python dicts preserve insertion order since 3.7, so json.dumps() without sort_keys=True may produce different output on different Python versions or when keys are inserted in different orders.
vectors.implementation_notes: Always use sort_keys=True (Python), keys().sort() (JS), or equivalent. Key ordering must be pure ASCII/byte ordering.

vectors.description: WRONG: canonical JSON with indent/whitespace — spaces change the hash
vectors.trap: json.dumps() defaults to separators=(', ', ': ') in Python (note spaces). Canonical JSON requires separators=(',', ':') — no spaces.
vectors.implementation_notes: Use separators=(',', ':') in Python. In JS, JSON.stringify(obj) with no space argument. Verify no whitespace between tokens.

vectors.description: WRONG: Unicode chars left as UTF-8 instead of \uXXXX escaped — different bytes, different hash
vectors.trap: In Python, json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) writes raw UTF-8. Canonical JSON requires ensure_ascii=True. In JS, JSON.stringify() does NOT escape non-ASCII by default — you must post-process.
vectors.implementation_notes: Python: ensure_ascii=True. JS: JSON.stringify() then replace non-ASCII with \uXXXX. Go: use json.Marshal which escapes by default.

vectors.description: WRONG: NFC-normalizing string values before hashing — the decomposed form (A + U+0300) and composed form (U+00C0) produce different hashes
vectors.trap: Some languages or libraries NFC-normalize input strings automatically. Canonical JSON must preserve the original byte sequence. Do NOT normalize before hashing.
vectors.implementation_notes: The detection layer uses NFKC + TR39 confusable resolution for signal matching. The canonical JSON layer must NOT normalize. These are separate concerns.
